text:
maria-api: Quick Q — as we start rolling the 'default model pin' change next week, what should external clients expect? Will we send a deprecation warning first, and how will fallbacks behave?

alex-plat: Short answer: yes, we plan a staged rollout + deprecation window. Long answer below.

sam-rl: timeline? and does this affect streaming/chunking behavior?

alex-plat: timeline: canary -> orgs above usage threshold -> full rollout over ~6 weeks. We won't change streaming semantics. This is purely model/version selection at routing time.

jess-runbooks: For comms: do we want an HTTP header or response field to indicate the model that served the request? Customers asked for that.

alex-plat: Agreed. We'll add a stable response header: `x-redwood-model-version` with the model id we actually executed against. Also a `x-redwood-model-pinned: true|false` during the migration window.

maria-api: Nice. Will SDKs automatically respect a server-side pin, or should clients pass an explicit header to opt into pinned behavior early?

alex-plat: SDKs keep current behavior by default (server chooses). We'll add an opt-in client header `Prefer: rw-model-pin=opt-in` for early adopters and `Prefer: rw-model-pin=force` for customers who want to force pinned variant (will be allowed only for teams on dedicated/private or with explicit permissions).

sam-rl: Fallbacks: if pinned model is unavailable (OOM, capacity), do we fall back to previous unpinned default or return an error? We need deterministic behavior for our SLOs.

alex-plat: Fallback policy: 1) If pinned model fails due to infra, try last-known-compatible variant (same major model family, lower size) within 200ms. 2) If no compatible variant available, fallback to the unpinned selection path (which may pick a different model). We will surface a header when a fallback happened: `x-redwood-model-fallback: <reason>` (e.g., `capacity`, `timeout`, `incompatible-kv`).

jess-runbooks: Can we have a short code snippet for clients to detect fallback?

alex-plat: sure — example: 
```
// Node fetch example
const res = await fetch(url, opts)
const pinned = res.headers.get('x-redwood-model-pinned') === 'true'
const model = res.headers.get('x-redwood-model-version')
const fallback = res.headers.get('x-redwood-model-fallback') // null if no fallback
if (fallback) { // log + maybe metric }
```

maria-api: Good. Any backward-compat pitfalls for response shapes? We must guarantee no additive / breaking changes to fields during this rollout.

alex-plat: Correct — we will not change the response schema as part of pinning. Model internals may generate slightly different token sequences, but the JSON shape is unchanged. For structured output we recommend customers pin their eval prompts and run a quick qa set before switching.

eng-sre: Infra note: canary will be targeted at us-east-1 and eu-west-1 low-traffic orgs first. We need to reserve some warm capacity for fallback variants so we don't cascade. Will coordinate capacity reservations with capacity planner.

sam-rl: For deprecation window: how long do we keep the old unpinned-default behavior available before turning it off? Customers want at least 60 days to migrate.

alex-plat: Proposal: 90-day deprecation window. Week 0: announcement + docs + SDK flags. Week 1-4: canary. Week 5-8: opt-in orgs. Week 9-12: broad rollout + metrics watch. Close after day 90 but we will extend if major customers request it.

maria-api: Sounds reasonable. For breaking-change comms: new banner in Console, API changelog entry, and an email to org admins scheduled at onboarding. Also we should add an API-level banner header `x-redwood-deprecation-info` for the first 14 days after the canary starts.

jess-runbooks: I'll draft the runbook and comms templates. Will add a checklist: update SDK, add header parsing, update migration guide, run evals.

upgrade-bot: [automated] Canary flag `model_pin_rollout` enabled for orgs: test-org-a, infra-experiments.

maria-api: Thanks — one last Q: how do we version the contract if we later change behavior (not just pinning) — semver header or v2 endpoint?

alex-plat: We keep API surface stable; for any breaking contract change we will publish a `x-redwood-api-version: 2` header and a new major flag in the SDK. Breaking changes will follow the same rollout + 90-day deprecation notice. Prefer header-based negotiation over a new path to avoid fragmentation.

sam-rl: ack. I'll add a CI check to ensure any PR that modifies response schemas includes migration notes and a changelog entry.

maria-api: Great — thanks everyone. Jess, ping me when the runbook draft is ready and I'll schedule the announcement for Monday. :thumbsup:

jess-runbooks: will do, aim to share by EOD tomorrow.

alex-plat: I'll open the tracking RFC and the header/SDK tickets after this thread.

upgrade-bot: [automated] Ticket created: RW-PLATFORM-1842 "Model pinning: headers + SDK opt-in"

eng-sre: noted, reserving fallback capacity window for canary.

maria-api: closing the loop — thanks all!
